:::{#thm-equivalence-iff}
#### Equivalence is a tautological biconditional

For [propositions](#def-proposition) $A$ and $B$,
$A$ and $B$ are [logically equivalent](#def-logically-equivalent)
exactly when $A \Leftrightarrow B$ is a [tautology](#def-tautology).

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

::: proof

By the definition of [if and only if](#def-iff),
$A \Leftrightarrow B$ is true in a row of the [truth table](#def-truth-table)
exactly when $A$ and $B$ have the same truth value in that row. <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
So $A \Leftrightarrow B$ is true in every row
exactly when $A$ and $B$ have the same truth value in every row,
which is the definition of $A \equiv B$.

:::

:::
